title: Choose the visual world for MCSS-Lite
question: The roll assigned Packing Manifest. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Packing Manifest
options.lineage: freight manifests, thermal shipping labels and customs inspection stamps
options.thesis: The design system as a shipping manifest: every part declared, labeled and inspected before it ships.
options.viewport: A full-width manifest label: MCSS-Lite as the consignee block, blocks as numbered line items, and a live validate stamp rejecting an invented class.
options.risk: Turns into costume if the label fields become decoration instead of real structure; product UI built on it must stay calm.

raised.raise: Every state carries a mark as well as a hue (struck rule, dashed outline, hatch), so no state depends on color.
Everything snaps to one ruled field pitch; rank comes from how many fields a box spans, not from type size.
Every part prints its own identifier: the class name sits in the field corner like a label field code.
One manifest drives every surface: editing a token in the demo reprints the whole page in lockstep.

options.label: Component Datasheet
options.lineage: IC datasheets: pinout diagrams, absolute maximum ratings, electrical characteristics tables
options.thesis: Each block documented like a chip: pinout for elements, ratings for constraints, a characteristics table for states.
options.viewport: A datasheet front page: part number MCSS-LITE, a pinout of c-button, and a ratings table of its states.
options.risk: The most familiar engineering-docs look; many developer tools already land here.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Layouts assemble components step by step, the way an instruction book seats each brick.
options.viewport: Step 1 to 3: an empty l-stack, a c-card clicking into it, then a c-button seated in l-cluster, with a parts inventory up front.
options.case: Fuses well: the Golden Rule becomes 'layouts seat the parts'; holds audience identification but explains the contract less directly than a manifest.
options.risk: Toy-like sky blue fights product UI that consumers build on these tokens.

options.label: Patent Drawing Sheet
options.thesis: Each block drawn as an exploded figure whose reference numerals link to lines of its contract.
options.viewport: Fig. 1, c-card exploded into header, title, body and footer, each numeral linked to its line in card.json.
options.case: Fuses strongly on product clarity (numerals map to contracts); weaker on audience identification for app builders.
options.risk: Line-art austerity can feel academic; the carmine must stay reserved for what is under inspection.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Zone-ramp neutrals with hatch density as state.
options.viewport: Stacked translucent sheets over an eleven-step ramp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: design-system readers do not identify with darkroom printing.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: A perforated rail of frames with tape-flag states.
options.viewport: A select rail crossing an orange field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: linear film metaphor fights a catalogue of parts.
options.kept: One fixed module pitch; rank by span.
options.risk: Orange-on-black is too loud for a UI kit.

options.label: Miura Fold Sheet
options.thesis: A packet that unfolds into a crease field.
options.viewport: A compact packet deploying into a tessellated sheet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: folding does not explain contracts or validation.

options.label: Generative Identity
options.thesis: A seed-driven mark that reshapes palette and layout.
options.viewport: A live mark reseeding the page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a contract system is deterministic; randomness undercuts trust.
options.kept: One source updates every surface in lockstep.
options.risk: Reads as a generic AI-brand trope.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean design-system docs site, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, a component preview and its code snippet.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other design-system site by design.
